## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

class ControlType(IntEnum):
    """Non-printable control codes which typically translate to ANSI codes."""

    BELL = 1
    CARRIAGE_RETURN = 2
    HOME = 3
    CLEAR = 4
    SHOW_CURSOR = 5
    HIDE_CURSOR = 6
    ENABLE_ALT_SCREEN = 7
    DISABLE_ALT_SCREEN = 8
    CURSOR_UP = 9

    CURSOR_BACKWARD = 12
    CURSOR_MOVE_TO_COLUMN = 13
    CURSOR_MOVE_TO = 14
    ERASE_IN_LINE = 15
    SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16


ControlCode = Union[
    Tuple[ControlType],
    Tuple[ControlType, Union[int, str]],
    Tuple[ControlType, int, int],
]


@rich_repr()
class Segment(NamedTuple):
    """A piece of text with associated style. Segments are produced by the Console render process and
    are ultimately converted in to strings to be written to the terminal.

    Args:
        text (str): A piece of text.
        style (:class:`~rich.style.Style`, optional): An optional style to apply to the text.
        control (Tuple[ControlCode], optional): Optional sequence of control codes.

    Attributes:
        cell_length (int): The cell length of this Segment.
    """

    text: str
    style: Optional[Style] = None
    control: Optional[Sequence[ControlCode]] = None

    @property
    def cell_length(self) -> int:
        """The number of terminal cells required to display self.text.

        Returns:
            int: A number of cells.
        """
        text, _style, control = self
        return 0 if control else cell_len(text)

    def __rich_repr__(self) -> Result:
        yield self.text
        if self.control is None:
            if self.style is not None:
                yield self.style
        else:
            yield self.style
            yield self.control

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        """Check if the segment contains text."""
        return bool(self.text)

    @property
    def is_control(self) -> bool:
        """Check if the segment contains control codes."""
        return self.control is not None

    @classmethod
    @lru_cache(1024 * 16)
    def _split_cells(cls, segment: "Segment", cut: int) -> Tuple["Segment", "Segment"]:
        text, style, control = segment
        _Segment = Segment

        cell_length = segment.cell_length
        if cut >= cell_length:
            return segment, _Segment("", style, control)

        cell_size = get_character_cell_size

        pos = int((cut / cell_length) * (len(text) - 1))

        before = text[:pos]
        cell_pos = cell_len(before)
        if cell_pos == cut:
            return (
                _Segment(before, style, control),
                _Segment(text[pos:], style, control),
            )
        while pos < len(text):
            char = text[pos]
            pos += 1
            cell_pos += cell_size(char)
            before = text[:pos]
            if cell_pos == cut:
                return (
                    _Segment(before, style, control),
                    _Segment(text[pos:], style, control),
                )
            if cell_pos > cut:
                return (
                    _Segment(before[: pos - 1] + " ", style, control),
                    _Segment(" " + text[pos:], style, control),
                )

        raise AssertionError("Will never reach here")

    def split_cells(self, cut: int) -> Tuple["Segment", "Segment"]:

from rich.segment import Segment
from rich.cells import cell_len

def test_split_cells():
    # \u20B7 is a wide character (width 2)
    text = "A\u20B7B"
    segment = Segment(text)
    print(f"Text: {text}, Cell length: {segment.cell_length}")
    
    # cut = 1: split after 'A'
    s1, s2 = Segment._split_cells(segment, 1)
    print(f"Cut 1: '{s1.text}' | '{s2.text}'")
    
    # cut = 2: split in the middle of \u20B7
    s1, s2 = Segment._split_cells(segment, 2)
    print(f"Cut 2: '{s1.text}' | '{s2.text}'")
    
    # cut = 3: split after \u20B7
    s1, s2 = Segment._split_cells(segment, 3)
    print(f"Cut 3: '{s1.text}' | '{s2.text}'")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_split_cells()
